For OIML CS, scheme A involves testing by the issuing authority, scheme B is... Actually, the OIML Certificate System: certificates issued under the "basic system" — the MAA (Mutual Acceptance Arrangement) has two schemes: A and B. This one mentions "OIML — MUTUAL ACCEPTANCE ARRANGEMENT" at the bottom, and NMi Certin B.V. is an OIML Issuing Authority NL1. MAA certificates are typically scheme A (the Issuing Authority performs evaluation) or scheme B (issuing authority reviews manufacturer's documentation). The cert says "This Certificate attests the conformity... represented by the sample(s) identified in the OIML Test Report" and lists test reports by NMi. This suggests scheme A. Hmm, but honestly it's ambiguous. Most R76 certificates are scheme A. I'll go with "A".
